effect_estimate.comment: Quantitative findings consist of descriptive city-level BCI scores (11 cities) and unadjusted bivariate correlation coefficients across 70 cities without confidence intervals or p-values; primary 3-city GCF Likert ratings in Table 4 evaluate flood-risk governance specifically.
effect_estimate.value: Across 11 Asian cities, the Blue City Index (BCI, 0–10 geometric mean of 25 urban water cycle indicators) ranged from 2.0 to 8.1: Jakarta (2.0), Ho Chi Minh City (2.4), Bandung (2.6), Bangkok (2.6), Manila (2.6), Ahmedabad (3.0), Taipei (3.9), Tianjin (4.9), Hohhot (5.0), Seoul (7.3), and Singapore (8.1), with low-BCI cities struggling to provide drinking water and sanitation in slums and experiencing up to 48% water leakage (Jakarta). Across 70 cities globally, BCI correlated positively with World Bank government effectiveness (r = 0.80), climate readiness index (r = 0.80), and GDP per capita (r = 0.70), and negatively with the Trends and Pressures Index (r = -0.79; CIs and p-values not reported). In the 3-city GCF flood-risk assessment, statutory compliance was limiting (-) in Ahmedabad and Bandung and neutral (0) in Taipei, policy evaluation was limiting (-) in all 3 cities, and stakeholder inclusiveness was limiting (-) in Bandung.
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF p. 6, Table 4; PDF pp. 7–9, Results and Fig. 3; PDF p. 10, Discussion and Fig. 4

mechanism_certainty.comment: Capped below 3 by non-experimental mixed-methods design. Rated 1 (documented association) rather than 2 because for drinking water and sanitation access outcomes, the study reports aggregate cross-city/cross-country indicator associations (e.g., BCI correlation r = 0.80 with government effectiveness; city-level BCI profiles; World Bank slum vs. WASH plots) and secondary literature synthesis, whereas the primary empirical stakeholder-interview governance assessment (GCF) in this paper focused specifically on flood risk management rather than directly observing legal/administrative water or sanitation access mechanisms.
mechanism_certainty.where_found: PDF p. 3, Introduction; PDF p. 6, Table 4; PDF pp. 7–13, Results and Discussion (Figs. 3–5)

sample_size.comment: Eleven Asian cities were purposively selected for TPF (12 indicators) and CBF (25 indicators) assessment; 3 of these cities (Ahmedabad, Bandung, Taipei) received in-depth GCF assessment via desk study and local stakeholder interviews (exact interviewee count is not reported in this article). Discussion Fig. 4 correlates BCI across 70 cities globally (and notes n = 15 cities globally assessed with GCF to date, insufficient for correlation).

study_design.comment: Authors describe the design as an 'empirical, comparative case study approach' applying the three-part City Blueprint Approach: quantitative secondary-data indicator scoring (TPF 0–4 and CBF 0–10 geometric mean Blue City Index) and Pearson correlations, paired with qualitative stakeholder interviews and policy/literature desk review scored on 27 Likert-scale GCF indicators in 3 cities.
study_design.value: Mixed-methods comparative multi-city case study combining quantitative diagnostic indicator assessment (Trends and Pressures Framework and City Blueprint Framework across 11 cities, plus cross-city bivariate correlations across 70 cities) with triangular qualitative-to-ordinal governance capacity assessment (desk study, in-depth stakeholder interviews, and interviewee feedback in 3 cities)
